analysis.title: Boring is Beautiful: Consumer Staples Too Strong to Ignore
key_insights: BTIG's technical strategist Jonathan Krinsky is warming up to Consumer Staples. XLP is breaking out of a multi-month base in absolute and relative terms, and staples are up 10% in the past month and 15% off the lows.

S&P 500 Staples beat S&P Tech by 33% over the last 30 days, the largest such move in about 25 years. The only comparable stretch was April 2000 through October 2001, after which staples beat tech by nearly 1000 bps over the next two years.

Sentiment on staples is quite bearish because they are seen as expensive with little growth. BTIG calls negative sentiment paired with strong price action a powerful set-up, and says staples are not particularly extended.

Tech (QQQ and SOXX) has fallen below a significant volume zone, so rallies into it are likely to meet overhead supply, as happened last Thursday. Strong support sits near $630, about 6% below current prices.
Semis were rejected below supply. BTIG thinks they need to trade back to their April breakout point, which implies about 17-25% more downside from current levels.

Historical analog: after the March 2000 dot-com peak, seven S&P sectors gained 12% or more over the following year and Consumer Staples rose over 50%. BTIG notes 2000 differs because many sectors were down 20-30% into that peak, but the defensive leadership is hard to ignore.

Memory names were widely called cheap in June, yet a broad basket of them fell about 50%. BTIG uses this to argue that cheap and expensive are subjective and that price action matters more than valuation.
Equal-weight Staples (RSPS) vs Discretionary (RSPD) has based for two years. A breakout through .58 in the ratio would be meaningful, though BTIG says it is premature to call a new uptrend.
COST is up 25% off its lows but roughly flat since early 2025, so near-term consolidation is possible. A measured move targets about $1300.

MDLZ is breaking a multi-year downtrend and CL is nearing a multi-year base breakout. BATS LN is called a pre-breakout idea and BF/B an unloved name nearing a breakout, with one buy and five sell ratings on the Street.

AAPL hit 52-week highs on back-to-back days but closed more than 1% below the high each day, which BTIG reads as upside exhaustion. In the last 20 years there were nine prior similar instances, with 20-day returns negative 89% of the time (average -12.57%, median -8.97%). BTIG sees AAPL, up 31% YTD, as vulnerable to downside reversion over the coming weeks.

The US Dollar Index is breaking out of a two-year trading range. BTIG calls it one of the most bullish charts it can find and probably not conducive to a risk-on environment. GBP/USD, AUD/USD, CAD/USD and NZD/USD look vulnerable.
BTIG still expects correlations to rise, so staples will not be fully immune to a broad-based decline.

tension_points.bull_case: Staples are breaking out of a multi-month base in absolute and relative terms. Sentiment is bearish and they are not extended. In 2000-01 staples beat tech by nearly 1000 bps over two years after a similar relative surge.
tension_points.bear_case: Staples are seen as expensive with little growth, and correlations typically rise in a broad-based decline. 2000 differs because sectors were already down 20-30% into that peak. COST is up 25% off the lows and may consolidate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A breakout in the RSPS/RSPD ratio through .58 would confirm a new staples uptrend. The report gives no explicit level that would invalidate the staples call.
